title: 8th Pay Commission: Understanding the ₹45,000 Pension Demand
description: The Bharat Pensioners Samaj has formally demanded a minimum monthly pension of ₹45,000 for central government retirees under the upcoming 8th Pay Commission. .

faq.q: When is the 8th Pay Commission expected to be constituted?
faq.a: While there's no official date yet, Pay Commissions are typically constituted every ten years. The 7th Pay Commission's recommendations were implemented in 2016, so the 8th Pay Commission is generally anticipated to be formed around 2024-2025, with recommendations implemented by 2026-2027.

faq.q: Who will benefit from the 8th Pay Commission's recommendations?
faq.a: The recommendations of the 8th Pay Commission will primarily benefit central government employees and pensioners. State government employees and pensioners often see similar revisions in their respective states, though this is decided independently by each state.

faq.q: How is pension currently calculated for central government retirees?
faq.a: Under the 7th Pay Commission, pension is generally calculated as 50% of the last drawn basic pay, subject to a minimum of ₹9,000 per month. This is further adjusted with Dearness Relief (DR), which is similar to Dearness Allowance (DA) for serving employees.

faq.q: Is the ₹45,000 minimum pension demand likely to be accepted?
faq.a: It's difficult to predict. The Bharat Pensioners Samaj's demand is a proposal, and the 8th Pay Commission will consider various factors, including financial implications, before making its recommendations. Past commissions have often significantly increased minimum pensions, but a five-fold jump would be substantial.

faq.q: Will the revised pension be taxable?
faq.a: Yes, pension income for government retirees is generally taxable under the head "Salaries" as per the Income Tax Act. Any increase in pension would therefore be subject to the applicable income tax slabs.
